$comment: Ground truth for the bmad-testarch-automate behavioral eval. It was authored from
voucher-service/docs/stories/6-6-voucher-redemption.md, from vouchers.js's own catalog
of rules, and from the seeded regression qualification.json records (the minimum-spend
boundary flipped from inclusive to exclusive). No bmad-testarch-automate run produced
any value in this file: every spec file under cases/ is hand-authored, standing in for
what a real run could produce against the fixed implementation.
Each case declares, per test, the outcome the fixed implementation must produce and the
outcome the mutated implementation must produce. Where the mutated outcome is "fail",
attributionPattern is the literal text Playwright's own toEqual() diff prints when the
mutation flips that redemption from accepted to rejected: the rejected body's own
reason, "below-minimum-spend", which the fixed body never carries. A test whose
attributionPattern would match for any other reason is not attributing the failure to
the seeded boundary and this corpus does not claim it does.
vacuousPattern and duplicateOfTitle are checked statically, against the test's own
source text, by test/eval-automate.js's validateCorpus: the pattern must be found
inside the named test's own body, and a declared duplicate's body must be textually
identical (whitespace collapsed) to the test it duplicates. Both are checked before any
server starts, the same way the atdd corpus's declaredPattern is checked against the
story before any scaffold runs.
detectsRegression is true for exactly one case, correct-run: the only spec set that
tests the boundary itself, cartTotal exactly equal to a voucher's minimumSpend. The
other three cases each stand in for a different way generated coverage can look
thorough and still fail to catch the regression: interior-only assertions, an assertion
that cannot fail against real behavior, and a duplicated assertion that adds nothing
beyond the test it repeats.
